statement: Anangu patch burning uses small, cool-season burns to create a mosaic of burnt and unburnt country; public management sources explain that this reduces fuel for large summer wildfires, encourages fresh growth and bush foods, and creates habitat and food for animals.

sources.citation: Parks Australia, “Cultural burning at Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park” fact sheet.
Australian Government, Uluru–Kata Tjuta National Park World Heritage description, updated 16 Apr. 2026.

notes: Stored as natural/observational explanatory practice because the public sources explicitly connect burning conditions and spatial pattern to ecological outcomes. This does not separate the practice from Tjukurpa.
